title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI quality gating and metrics integration
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary: Add per-prompt quality gating to the eval-harness CI workflow and wire eval metrics into a blocking GitHub check. This PR introduces a lightweight gate implementation that validates candidate model changes against per-prompt thresholds (accuracy/coverage/fluency) and fails the CI check when any prompt in the configured prompt-sets regresses beyond tolerated deltas. Motivation: we've seen a few subtle prompt-set regressions slip through unit/integration tests and only get detected post-release via monitoring. Automated per-prompt gating in PR CI will catch regressions earlier and make rollouts safer.

What this change does (high level):
- New CI check action (.github/workflows/eval-harness-ci.yml) that runs eval-harness in PR mode and posts a dedicated check named "eval-harness/prompt-gate".
- Adds eval_harness/ci/per_prompt_gate.py which loads prompt-level thresholds from eval_config/prompt_thresholds.yaml, computes delta vs baseline metrics, and emits a pass/fail result with a concise failure summary.
- Threshold config (eval_config/prompt_thresholds.yaml): per-prompt metric thresholds and tolerated delta percentages. Ship with default curated thresholds for customer-facing prompt-sets.
- Integrates with existing eval artifacts: uses the baseline artifact uploaded to S3/artifacts by nightly-run workflow and the current PR run output to compute diffs. Fallback behavior if baseline missing: non-blocking (warn) to avoid false-positives on new prompt-sets.
- Tests: unit tests for gate logic (tests/eval/test_per_prompt_gate.py) and a small e2e smoke test that validates the workflow step using a local mocked artifact.
- Docs: docs/eval/ci_gates.md explains the gating model and guidance for setting thresholds.

Why this approach: per-prompt thresholds let us catch regressions that are drowned out in aggregate metrics. Using a CI check makes the gate visible in PR UI and allows engineers to iterate on thresholds quickly. The implementation is intentionally conservative: default thresholds are permissive, and gate failure messages include exact prompt and metric deltas to aid triage.

Backwards-compatibility and safety: The check is opt-in via the repo-level config at .github/eval-harness-config.yaml. For repos that enable the check, it's blocking by default for changes touching model-serving code or eval assets. We also include an admin override label (ci/eval-harness:allow-failure) to bypass the gate for emergency rollouts.

Related tickets: ENG-1245 (design per-prompt gating), ENG-2103 (CI integration), PM-78 (product impact review).

Notes on CI run history for this PR: Initial run (2026-02-19) failed due to a flaky artifact upload step; fixed in commit 2 by adding retry logic to the upload action. After the fix CI passed and the check reported synthesized failures for an intentionally regressed prompt in the test fixture (expected). The PR was reviewed, approved, and merged via squash on 2026-02-24.

changes_snippet:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: eval_harness/ci/per_prompt_gate.py
+def run_gate(baseline, current, thresholds):
+    """Compute per-prompt deltas and return failing prompts.
+    """
+    failures = []
+    for p in thresholds:
+        d = current[p]['accuracy'] - baseline[p]['accuracy']
+        if d < -thresholds[p]['accuracy_delta']:
+            failures.append((p, d))
+    return failures
*** End Patch
release_notes:
- Add per-prompt CI quality gating via eval-harness
- Integrate eval metrics into a blocking GitHub check (eval-harness/prompt-gate)
- Add default prompt-level thresholds and documentation
